proposals.before: After Yin died, his younger brother Cheng took the throne.
proposals.after: After Yin died, his younger brother Zhi took the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 陟 is Zhi, not Cheng; the packet romanizes the personal name incorrectly.

proposals.before: When Yin died, his younger brother Cheng seized the position.
proposals.after: When Yin died, his younger brother Zhi succeeded to the position.
proposals.reason: 陟 is Zhi; 襲位 means succeeded to the position, not seized.

proposals.before: In the third year of Zhenming he took an imperial title, named his state Great Han, adopted the era Gankeng, and performed suburban sacrifices.
proposals.after: In the third year of Zhenming he took an imperial title, named his state Great Han, adopted the era Qianheng, and performed suburban sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Southern Han era 乾亨 is Qianheng, not Gankeng.

proposals.before: In the third year of Zhenming he arrogated an imperial title; the state was called Great Han, the era name was Gankeng, and suburban sacrifices were performed.
proposals.after: In the third year of Zhenming he arrogated an imperial title; the state was called Great Han, the era name was Qianheng, and suburban sacrifices were performed.
proposals.reason: 乾亨 should be romanized Qianheng.

proposals.before: The inner attendant Chen Shouyan introduced the witch Fan Hu, who claimed the Jade Emperor had sent her to name Chang Crown Prince Emperor. Within the palace they hung silken curtains, displayed rare treasures, and set out a throne for the Jade Emperor.
proposals.after: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou introduced the witch Fan Hu, who claimed the Jade Emperor had sent her to name Chang Crown Prince Emperor. Within the palace they hung silken curtains, displayed rare treasures, and set out a throne for the Jade Emperor.
proposals.reason: 陳延壽 is Chen Yanshou; Shouyan reverses the given-name characters.

proposals.before: The inner attendant Chen Shouyan brought the shamaness Fan Hu into the palace, saying the Jade Emperor had sent Fan Hu to appoint Chang as Crown Prince Emperor; in the palace silken curtains were hung, rare treasures arrayed, and a seat for the Jade Emperor set up.
proposals.after: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou brought the shamaness Fan Hu into the palace, saying the Jade Emperor had sent Fan Hu to appoint Chang as Crown Prince Emperor; in the palace silken curtains were hung, rare treasures arrayed, and a seat for the Jade Emperor set up.
proposals.reason: 陳延壽 is Chen Yanshou, not Chen Shouyan.

proposals.before: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Shouyan had all been sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor and that he must not punish them even if they erred.
proposals.after: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou had all been sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor and that he must not punish them even if they erred.
proposals.reason: 延壽 short form should be Yanshou.

proposals.before: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Shouyan were all sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor, and that if they erred he must not punish them.
proposals.after: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou were all sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor, and that if they erred he must not punish them.
proposals.reason: 延壽 should be Yanshou.

proposals.before: Chen Shouyan devised all manner of lewd contrivances, spending tens of thousands in gold every day.
proposals.after: Chen Yanshou devised all manner of lewd contrivances, spending tens of thousands in gold every day.
proposals.reason: 陳延壽 is Chen Yanshou.

proposals.before: Chen Shouyan made all manner of lewd clever devices, spending tens of thousands in gold daily.
proposals.after: Chen Yanshou made all manner of lewd clever devices, spending tens of thousands in gold daily.
proposals.reason: 陳延壽 is Chen Yanshou.

proposals.before: Yu then sent his Director of the Office of Personnel, Gong Shenyi, with another letter that read:
proposals.after: Yu then sent his Supervising Secretary, Gong Shenyi, with another letter that read:
proposals.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Director of the Office of Personnel.

proposals.before: Yu again sent his Director of the Office of Personnel Gong Shenyi with a letter saying:
proposals.after: Yu again sent his Supervising Secretary Gong Shenyi with a letter saying:
proposals.reason: 給事中 is mistranslated as Director of the Office of Personnel.

proposals.before: Yesterday the Great Dynasty marched south to recover Chu territory; since arms were joined, a breach has formed.
proposals.after: Recently the Great Dynasty marched south to recover Chu territory; since arms were joined, a breach has formed.
proposals.reason: Classical 昨 here means 'recently / the other day,' not calendar yesterday; the idiomatic line already has the correct sense, so the literal should not force 'Yesterday.'

proposals.before: No terrain was more perilous than Jian'ge, yet Yong and Shu are already lost;
proposals.after: No state was more perilous than Jian'ge, yet Yong and Shu are already lost;
proposals.reason: Source 國莫險於劍閣 parallels 兵莫強於上黨 and means no state was more secure in perilous terrain than at Jian'ge; 'terrain' drops the state subject.

proposals.before: These are the deeds of sages and worthies — what shame could there be in refusing them?
proposals.after: These are the deeds of sages and worthies — what shame could there be in not doing them?
proposals.reason: Chinese 何恥而不為哉 asks what shame there is in not practicing these deeds; 'refusing them' reverses the sense.

proposals.before: Chang sent the great general Wu Yanrou with troops to relieve He; Mei and the others set ambush troops on the southern bank of Xiang.
proposals.after: Chang sent the great general Wu Yanrou with troops to relieve He; Mei and the others set ambush troops on the southern bank.
proposals.reason: Chinese 南鄉岸 does not name the Xiang; the literal invents 'of Xiang'.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month Mei and the others attacked Shao Prefecture; the commander-in-chief Li Chenguo drew up an army of tens of thousands below Lianhua Mountain.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Mei and the others attacked Shao Prefecture; the commander-in-chief Li Chengwo drew up an army of tens of thousands below Lianhua Mountain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李承渥 is Chengwo; Chenguo is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Now they met Mei, who gathered every powerful crossbow in the army and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants stampeded, their riders fell, and they trampled Chenguo's army in turn — utter defeat; Chenguo barely escaped with his life.
proposals.after: Now they met Mei, who gathered every powerful crossbow in the army and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants stampeded, their riders fell, and they trampled Chengwo's army in turn — utter defeat; Chengwo barely escaped with his life.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic Chenguo conflicts with 承渥 / Chengwo for the same person.

proposals.before: Now they met Mei; Mei gathered every powerful crossbow in the army and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants ran and stamped, riders all fell, and trampled Chenguo's army in reverse — utter defeat; Chenguo barely escaped with his life.
proposals.after: Now they met Mei; Mei gathered every powerful crossbow in the army and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants ran and stamped, riders all fell, and trampled Chengwo's army in reverse — utter defeat; Chengwo barely escaped with his life.
proposals.reason: Literal Chenguo conflicts with Chinese 承渥.

proposals.before: Chang feared it was poisoned wine and wept, saying, "Your subject inherited my grandfather's realm, defied the Song court, and brought the imperial army down upon me — a crime that surely deserved death. Your Majesty spared my life; now that I live to see peace, it is enough to be an ordinary subject of Great Liang.
proposals.after: Chang feared it was poisoned wine and wept, saying, "Your subject inherited my grandfather's realm, defied the Han court, and brought the imperial army down upon me — a crime that surely deserved death. Your Majesty spared my life; now that I live to see peace, it is enough to be an ordinary subject of Great Liang.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 韓廷; idiomatic invents 'Song court' rather than rendering the source wording.

proposals.before: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the hundred officials to welcome them, but was blocked by Guo Chongyue.
proposals.after: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the hundred officials to welcome them, but they were blocked by Guo Chongyue.
proposals.reason: Passive 'was blocked' misassigns the subject; 為郭崇嶽所遏 refers to Baoxing's welcoming party.

proposals.before: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu received the titles of Grand Mentor, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General, then Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor. Every matter of war and state passed through his hands.
proposals.after: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General, then Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor. Every matter of war and state passed through his hands.
proposals.reason: 特進 is the honorific rank Special Advancement, not Grand Mentor (太師); the idiomatic English conflates the two.

proposals.before: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu was given the special advancement of Grand Mentor, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and General Who Quells Disturbances on Horseback; he was then changed to Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor — all military and state affairs were decided by Chengshu.
proposals.after: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu was given Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General; he was then changed to Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor — all military and state affairs were decided by Chengshu.
proposals.reason: 驃騎大將軍 is Cavalry Grand General, not General Who Quells Disturbances on Horseback; 特進 is also mistranslated as Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: He received the titles of Grand Mentor, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, Army Observer of the Six Armies, and Acting Inner Captain, then rose to Cavalry Grand General and Inner Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, Army Observer of the Six Armies, and Acting Inner Captain, then rose to Cavalry Grand General and Inner Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: 特進 is again rendered as Grand Mentor instead of Special Advancement.

proposals.before: When Chang took the throne, Chongyu became Inner Captain, received the titles of Grand Mentor and Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and was appointed Secretary of Inspection Bureau Affairs.
proposals.after: When Chang took the throne, Chongyu became Inner Captain, received Special Advancement and Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and was appointed Secretary of Inspection Bureau Affairs.
proposals.reason: 特進 is Special Advancement, not Grand Mentor.
